newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma pierces 310, depos, forwards spike.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma pierces 310, depos, forwards spike.

text.p: Ecu/drachma broke the 310 level on the upside on ecu buying from London-based banks in lively trading, likely linked to Tuesday's bond auction, forex dealers said.
Depos and forex forwards spiked 20 to 40 basis points on funding for bonds auctioned yesterday and uncertainty over the amount the central bank is going to drain in today's depo tender, dealers said.

"We see some concerted drachma selling for ecus from London-based banks for good sums," said a forex dealer. "Ecu/drachma opened at 309.90/95, eased to 309.75/80 and then headed upwards, breaking above 310."
Dealers said a possible explanation for the firmer ecu/drachma was position squaring by foreign investors who did not get what they expected from Tuesday's bond auction.
Mark/drachma was also trading higher, breaking the 157 level on the upside.

Depos and forex forwards were also up with the rise more accentuated in short tenors and dealers attributed the rate spike to funding for bonds and uncertainty over the amount the central bank is going to drain today in its depo tender.
The Bank of Greece offered to drain an unspecified amount of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular depo tender on Wednesday.
Cut-off prices at Greece's auction of five-, seven- and 10-year bonds on Tuesday were 98.26, 96.2 and 96.03 respectively.

"The outcome of the auction was expected and accepted bids were lower than in previous auctions," said a senior dealer at a private bank. "Fixed coupon bonds have only to gain if the central bank sticks to its tight monetary policy."
The negative of cost carry would lead to short-term losses but the potential for large capital gains in the long haul was present, the dealer said.
"The same bonds will trade above par, possibly around 101, this time next year," he said.
Prices of 10-year bonds were trading around 95.50/70, dealers said.
Greece sought bids for 75 billion drachmas each of five- and seven-year bonds with coupons of 9.2 percent and 8.9 percent respectively, and 120 billion drachmas of 8.8 percent, 10-year bonds.
The five- and seven-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on March 19 and then bids were re-opened on June 17. The 10-year bonds were auctioned for the first time ever on June 17.
Greece will also auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes on July 29.
Bids of 167 billion drachnas, 123 billion and 233 billion were submitted for five-, seven- and 10-year bonds at the auction.
The mark was quoted at 156.88/98 from Tuesday's 156.700 fix, the dollar at 281.04/14 drachmas from 281.020 and the ecu at 309.53/63 from 309.55 drachmas.
